{{SupportPage|vendor=NETGEAR|model=WPN311|vs_id=2621}}, [http://support.netgear.com/app/answers/detail/a_id/872 Driver] This device is clearly a [[Cameo WLG-1202|'''Cameo''' WLG-1202]]. "NETGEAR" and "32-bit Wireless PCI Adapter Rev.A3" (as well as a large bit of FCC compliance text, some other stuff, the FCC ID, and the IC ID) is silkscreened on the board. A label on the back of the board identifies the device as a WPN311 V1H2. This device is presumed to use AR2414 based on the specifications. The FCC pictures of the card also indicate that is indeed an AR2414. [http://forums.whirlpool.net.au/archive/727946 A whirlpool.net.au user described a WPN311 card labeled with Rev. A3 on the back] [http://debianforum.de/forum/viewtopic.php?f=30&t=134648 ath5k dump (copied below)] 
 dmesg | grep ath5k
[   25.378627] ath5k 0000:00:0b.0: PCI INT A -> Link[LNKA] -> GSI 10 (level, low) -> IRQ 10
[   25.390695] ath5k 0000:00:0b.0: registered as 'phy0'
[   26.271140] ath5k phy0: Atheros AR2414 chip found (MAC: 0x79, PHY: 0x45)
